publications.title: Medtrinity-25m: A large-scale multimodal dataset with multigranular annotations for medicine
publications.authors: Y Xie*, C Zhou*, L Gao*, J Wu*, X Li, HY Zhou, S Liu, L Xing, J Zou, C Xie, ...
publications.abstract: We introduce MedTrinity-25M, a comprehensive large-scale multimodal dataset for medicine, covering over 25 million images across 10 modalities with multigranular annotations for more than 65 diseases, encompassing global information (modality, organ detection) and local information (ROI analysis, lesion texture, region-wise correlations). We develop the first automated pipeline that scales up multimodal data by generating image-ROI-description triplets without paired text descriptions, using domain-specific expert models and retrieval-augmented generation. We propose LLaVA-Tri by pretraining LLaVA on MedTrinity-25M, achieving SOTA on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA.

publications.title: Vuldetectbench: Evaluating the deep capability of vulnerability detection with large language models
publications.authors: Y Liu*, L Gao*, M Yang*, Y Xie, P Chen, X Zhang, W Chen
publications.abstract: LLMs have training corpora containing large amounts of program code. However, comprehensive research on detecting program vulnerabilities and evaluating LLMs in this specialized scenario is lacking. We introduce VulDetectBench, a benchmark designed to assess vulnerability detection capabilities of LLMs through five tasks of increasing difficulty (identify, classify, locate). Evaluating 17 open- and closed-source models, we find existing models achieve over 80% accuracy on identification/classification but fall short on detailed analysis tasks (under 30% accuracy). Publicly available.

publications.title: Shaping the Safety Boundaries: Understanding and Defending Against Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
publications.authors: L Gao, J Geng, X Zhang, P Nakov, X Chen
publications.abstract: Jailbreaking in LLMs is a major security concern. There is insufficient understanding of how jailbreaking works. We conduct a large-scale analysis of seven jailbreak methods and find disagreements stem from insufficient observation samples. We introduce the notion of a safety boundary, and find that jailbreaks shift harmful activations outside that boundary where LLMs are less sensitive to harmful information; the low and middle layers are critical in such shifts. Leveraging these insights we propose Activation Boundary Defense (ABD), which adaptively constrains activations within the safety boundary, using Bayesian optimization to selectively apply defense to low and middle layers. ABD achieves average DSR over 98% with less than 2% impact on general capabilities.

publications.title: Audio jailbreak: An open comprehensive benchmark for jailbreaking large audio-language models
publications.authors: Z Song, Q Jiang, M Cui, M Li, L Gao, Z Zhang, Z Xu, Y Wang, C Wang, ...
publications.abstract: The rise of Large Audio Language Models (LAMs) brings both potential and risks. We introduce AJailBench, the first benchmark specifically designed to evaluate jailbreak vulnerabilities in LAMs. We construct AJailBench-Base, a dataset of 1,495 adversarial audio prompts spanning 10 policy-violating categories, converted from textual jailbreak attacks using realistic TTS. We evaluate several SOTA LAMs and reveal none exhibit consistent robustness. We propose an Audio Perturbation Toolkit (APT) applying targeted distortions across time, frequency, and amplitude, enforcing a semantic consistency constraint and employing Bayesian optimization, yielding AJailBench-APT. Even small, semantically preserved perturbations significantly reduce safety performance of leading LAMs.

publications.title: Socialmaze: A benchmark for evaluating social reasoning in large language models
publications.authors: Z Xu, Y Wang, Y Huang, J Ye, H Zhuang, Z Song, L Gao, C Wang, Z Chen, ...
publications.abstract: Success in socially grounded tasks depends on a model's social reasoning ability. There is currently no systematic evaluation framework that comprehensively assesses social reasoning of LLMs. We introduce SocialMaze, a benchmark that systematically incorporates three core challenges: deep reasoning, dynamic interaction, and information uncertainty, across six tasks in three settings: social reasoning games, daily-life interactions, and digital community platforms. Evaluation reveals models vary substantially in handling dynamic interactions; chain-of-thought models perform better on deep inference; and reasoning degrades under uncertainty. Targeted fine-tuning on curated reasoning examples improves performance.

publications.title: DyFlow: Dynamic Workflow Framework for Agentic Reasoning
publications.authors: Y Wang, Z Xu, Y Huang, X Wang, Z Song, L Gao, C Wang, X Tang, ...
publications.abstract: Agent systems based on LLMs show potential in complex reasoning, but building efficient generalizable workflows remains challenging. We propose DyFlow, a dynamic workflow generation framework that adaptively constructs and adjusts reasoning procedures based on task requirements and real-time intermediate feedback. DyFlow consists of a designer that decomposes complex problems into sub-goals and dynamically plans next steps, and an executor that carries out operations using dynamic operators with context-aware parameterization. Evaluated across social reasoning, biomedical tasks, mathematical problem solving, and code generation, DyFlow significantly outperforms baselines with substantial Pass@k improvements and robust cross-domain generalization.

publications.title: Do LLMs" Feel"? Emotion Circuits Discovery and Control
publications.authors: C Wang, Y Zhang, R Yu, Y Zheng, L Gao, Z Song, Z Xu, G Xia, H Zhang, ...
publications.abstract: As demand for emotional intelligence in LLMs grows, a key challenge lies in understanding the internal mechanisms of emotional expression and controlling emotions. This study addresses: (1) Do LLMs contain context-agnostic mechanisms shaping emotional expression? (2) What form do they take? (3) Can they be harnessed for universal emotion control? We construct SEV (Scenario-Event with Valence) to elicit comparable internal states, extract context-agnostic emotion directions, and identify neurons and attention heads implementing emotional computation via analytical decomposition and causal analysis, validating causal roles via ablation and enhancement. We integrate local components into global emotion circuits. Directly modulating these circuits achieves 99.65% emotion-expression accuracy, surpassing prompting and steering. First systematic study to uncover and validate emotion circuits in LLMs.

publications.title: Word Form Matters: LLMs' Semantic Reconstruction under Typoglycemia
publications.authors: C Wang, T Gu, Z Wei, L Gao, Z Song, X Chen
publications.abstract: Human readers efficiently comprehend scrambled words (Typoglycemia), primarily by relying on word form. While advanced LLMs exhibit similar abilities, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We propose SemRecScore, a reliable metric to quantify semantic reconstruction, and study how word form and contextual information influence LLMs' reconstruction, identifying word form as the core factor. LLMs rely on specialized attention heads to extract and process word-form information, stable across scrambling levels. This distinction between LLMs' fixed word-form attention and human readers' adaptive strategy provides insights into enhancing LLM performance with human-like context-aware mechanisms.

publications.title: Adversarial Cooperative Rationalization: The Risk of Spurious Correlations in Even Clean Datasets
publications.authors: W Liu, Z Niu, L Gao, Z Deng, J Wang, H Wang, R Li
publications.abstract: This study investigates the self-rationalization framework constructed with a cooperative game, where a generator extracts the most informative segment and a predictor uses the selected subset. We uncover a caveat: such a cooperative game could unintentionally introduce a sampling bias during rationale extraction, creating an incorrect correlation between selected rationale and label even when semantically unrelated. We elucidate the origins using theoretical analysis and empirical evidence, and introduce an instruction to prevent the predictor from learning the correlations. On six text and two graph classification datasets across GRUs, BERT, and GCN, our method outperforms recent rationalization methods and achieves comparable or better results than llama3.1-8b-instruct.

publications.title: Evaluate bias without manual test sets: A concept representation perspective for llms
publications.authors: L Gao, K Wan, W Liu, C Wang, Z Song, Z Xu, Y Wang, V Stoyanov, ...
publications.abstract: Bias in LLMs undermines reliability and fairness. We focus on a common form: when two reference concepts (e.g., sentiment polarities) are asymmetrically correlated with a target concept, the model exhibits unintended bias. We propose BiasLens, a test-set-free bias analysis framework based on the structure of the model's vector space. BiasLens combines Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract interpretable concept representations, and quantifies bias by measuring variation in representational similarity between the target and each reference concept. Without labeled data, BiasLens shows strong agreement with traditional metrics (Spearman r > 0.85) and reveals biases hard to detect otherwise.

publications.title: Beyond Survival: Evaluating LLMs in Social Deduction Games with Human-Aligned Strategies
publications.authors: Z Song, Y Huang, J Liu, H Luo, C Wang, L Gao, Z Xu, M Han, X Chang, ...
publications.abstract: Social deduction games like Werewolf combine language, reasoning, and strategy. Most studies reduce the game to LLM self-play, yielding templated utterances. We curate a high-quality, human-verified multimodal Werewolf dataset with over 100 hours of video, 32.4M utterance tokens, and 15 rule variants. We propose a strategy-alignment evaluation using the winning faction's strategies as ground truth in two stages: speech evaluation (multiple-choice tasks assessing social ability across five dimensions) and decision evaluation (voting choices and opponent-role inferences). SOTA LLMs show diverse performance, roughly half below 0.50, revealing gaps in deception and counterfactual reasoning.

publications.title: A fano-style accuracy upper bound for llm single-pass reasoning in multi-hop qa
publications.authors: K Wan, L Gao, H Mu, P Nakov, Y Wang, X Chen
publications.abstract: Multi-Hop Question Answering requires integrating dispersed evidence through sequential reasoning under noise, challenging for LLMs with finite per-pass output capacity. Our analysis establishes a Fano-style accuracy upper bound, defining a theoretical performance ceiling for single-pass LLMs: accuracy inevitably collapses once task complexity exceeds model capacity. Building on these principles we introduce InfoQA, a proof-of-concept multi-call framework combining capacity-aware task decomposition with active pruning of prior reasoning traces, plus a dependency-explicit workflow. Experiments show model behavior aligns with predicted capacity curves while InfoQA achieves consistent improvements.

publications.title: M3MAD-Bench: Are Multi-Agent Debates Really Effective Across Domains and Modalities?
publications.authors: A Li, J Zhang, L Li, Y Duan, L Gao, M Chen, W Qin, S Li, F Ji, N Liu, L Cui, ...
publications.abstract: As an agent-level reasoning and coordination paradigm, Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) orchestrates multiple agents through structured debate to improve answer quality and support complex reasoning. However, existing research on MAD suffers from two fundamental limitations: evaluations are conducted under fragmented and inconsistent settings, hindering fair comparison, and are largely restricted to single-modality scenarios that rely on textual inputs only. To address these gaps, we introduce M3MAD-Bench, a unified and extensible benchmark for evaluating MAD methods across Multi-domain tasks, Multi-modal inputs, and Multi-dimensional metrics. M3MAD-Bench establishes standardized protocols over five core task domains: Knowledge, Mathematics, Medicine, Natural Sciences, and Complex Reasoning, and systematically covers both pure text and vision-language datasets, enabling controlled cross-modality comparison. We evaluate MAD methods on nine base models spanning different architectures, scales, and modality capabilities. Beyond accuracy, M3MAD-Bench incorporates efficiency-oriented metrics such as token consumption and inference time, providing a holistic view of performance-cost trade-offs. Extensive experiments yield systematic insights into the effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency of MAD across text-only and multimodal scenarios.

publications.title: Under the Shadow of Babel: How Language Shapes Reasoning in LLMs
publications.authors: C Wang, Y Zhang, L Gao, Z Xu, Z Song, Y Wang, X Chen
publications.abstract: If the structure of language shapes cognitive patterns, LLMs trained on human language may internalize habitual logical structures of different languages. We introduce BICAUSE, a structured bilingual dataset for causal reasoning with aligned Chinese and English samples in forward and reversed causal forms. Findings: (1) LLMs exhibit typologically aligned attention patterns, focusing more on causes and sentence-initial connectives in Chinese; (2) models internalize language-specific causal word-order preferences and rigidly apply them, degrading performance especially in Chinese; (3) when causal reasoning succeeds, representations converge toward semantically aligned abstractions across languages. LLMs internalize reasoning biases shaped by language.

publications.title: Gta: Graph theory agent and benchmark for algorithmic graph reasoning with llms
publications.authors: Z Xu, Y Wang, C Wang, L Gao, Z Song, Y Huang, Z Chen, X Zhang, ...

publications.title: ServImage: An Image Generation and Editing Benchmark from Real-world Commercial Imaging Services
publications.authors: F Ji, J Yang, Z Song, L Gao, J Liang, Z Chen, J Zhang, X Chen
publications.abstract: Recent image generation and editing models demonstrate robust adherence to instructions and high visual quality on academic benchmarks. However, their performance on paid, real-world design projects remains uncertain. We introduce ServImage, a benchmark that explicitly correlates model outputs with economic value in commercial design projects. ServImage consists of (i) ServImageBench: a dataset of 1.07k paid commercial design tasks and 2.05k designer deliverables totaling over $295k; (ii) ServImageScore: an integrated scoring system combining baseline requirements fulfilment, visual execution quality, and commercial necessity satisfaction; (iii) ServImageModel: a payment prediction model achieving 82.00% accuracy in predicting human payment decisions.

publications.title: When Personalization Tricks Detectors: The Feature-Inversion Trap in Machine-Generated Text Detection
publications.authors: L Gao, X Li, C Wang, M Li, W Liu, Z Song, J Zhang, R Yan, P Nakov, ...
publications.abstract: LLMs producing fluent text and imitating personal style heighten the risk of identity impersonation. No prior work examined personalized machine-generated text (MGT) detection. We introduce the first benchmark for evaluating detector robustness in personalized settings, built from literary and blog texts paired with LLM imitations. Results show large performance gaps: some SOTA detectors suffer significant drops. We attribute this to the feature-inversion trap, where features discriminative in general domains become inverted and misleading on personalized text. We propose a method to predict detector performance changes by identifying latent directions of inverted features and constructing probe datasets, accurately predicting direction and magnitude (85% correlation with actual gaps).

publications.title: One Model, Multiple Goals: Adaptive Multi-Objective Learning for E-commerce Dialogue Systems
publications.authors: M Li, J Xiang, E Zhou, L Gao, T Li, Q Zhang, X Zhang, X Chen
publications.abstract: Dialogue systems in e-commerce scenarios often need to satisfy multiple objectives: accurately reasoning over user profiles to ensure correct decision-making, while also generating natural and faithful responses. We propose MORE, an adaptive Multi-Objective REinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes reasoning accuracy and linguistic naturalness. Instead of optimizing a single mixed reward, we treat reasoning functions as constraints that guide policy optimization. At inference time the system generates responses without explicit reasoning steps. We introduce an adaptive multi-reward mechanism that aggregates signals such as fluency and naturalness and dynamically reweighs them via gradient feedback. We evaluate MORE on two real-world dialogue systems at ByteDance and MultiWOZ 2.2; in 14-day online experiments on ByteDance production traffic, MORE improves overall and reached conversion by 16.53% and 30.09%.

publications.title: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis for Language Model Steering
publications.authors: L Gao, J Zhang, W Liu, F Ji, C Wang, Z Song, A Ghosh, Y Mohamed, ...
publications.abstract: Steering is a widely used technique for controlling large language models, yet its effects are often unstable and hard to predict. Existing theoretical accounts are largely based on the Linear Representation Hypothesis (LRH). By relaxing LRH's orthogonality assumption while preserving linear representations, we show that overlapping concept contributions naturally yield a sample-specific axis-orthogonal structure. We formalize this as the Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis (CRH). In CRH, a central axis captures the main difference between concept absence and presence and drives concept generation; a surrounding normal plane controls steering sensitivity. Within this plane, only specific sensitive sectors strongly facilitate concept activation. The sensitive sector cannot be reliably identified from difference vectors, introducing intrinsic uncertainty that provides a principled explanation for why steering outcomes often fluctuate even with well-aligned directions. Experiments verify the cylindrical structure and demonstrate CRH interprets model steering behavior in real settings.
